chunks.text: 4 D ECISION MAKING TASKS

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: We also test ReAct on two language-based interactive decision-making tasks, ALFWorld and

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: WebShop, both of which feature complex environments that require agents to act over long horizons

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: with sparse rewards, warranting the need for reasoning to act and explore effectively.

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: ALFWorld ALFWorld (Shridhar et al., 2020b) (Figure 1(2)) is a synthetic text-based game designed

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: to align with the embodied ALFRED benchmark (Shridhar et al., 2020a). It includes 6 types of

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: tasks in which an agent needs to achieve a high-level goal (e.g. examine paper under desklamp) by

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: navigating and interacting with a simulated household via text actions (e.g. go to coffeetable 1, take

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: paper 2, use desklamp 1). A task instance can have more than 50 locations and take an expert policy

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: more than 50 steps to solve, thus challenging an agent to plan and track subgoals, as well as explore

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: systematically (e.g. check all desks one by one for desklamp). In particular, one challenge built into

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: ALFWorld is the need to determine likely locations for common household items (e.g. desklamps will

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: likely be on desks, shelfs, or dressers), making this environment a good ﬁt for LLMs to exploit their

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: pretrained commonsense knowledge. To prompt ReAct, we randomly annotate three trajectories

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: from the training set for each task type, where each trajectory includes sparse thoughts that (1)

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: decompose the goal, (2) track subgoal completion, (3) determine the next subgoal, and (4) reason via

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: commonsense where to ﬁnd an object and what to do with it. We show prompts used for ALFWorld

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: in Appendix C.4. Following Shridhar et al. (2020b), we evaluate on 134 unseen evaluation games

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: in a task-speciﬁc setup. For robustness, we construct 6 prompts for each task type through each

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: permutation of 2 annotated trajectories from the 3 we annotate. Act prompts are constructed using

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: the same trajectories, but without thoughts — since task instances are randomly chosen from the

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: training set, it favors neitherReAct nor Act and provides a fair and controlled comparison to test the

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: importance of sparse thoughts. For baselines, we use BUTLER (Shridhar et al., 2020b), an imitation

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: learning agent trained on 105 expert trajectories for each task type5.

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: WebShop Can ReAct also interact with noisy real-world language environments for practical

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: applications? We investigate WebShop (Yao et al., 2022), a recently proposed online shopping

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: website environment with 1.18M real-world products and 12k human instructions. Unlike ALFWorld,

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: Webshop contains a high variety of structured and unstructured texts (e.g. product titles, descriptions,

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: and options crawled from Amazon), and requires an agent to purchase a product based on a user

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: instruction (e.g. “I am looking for a nightstand with drawers. It should have a nickel ﬁnish, and

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: priced lower than $140”) through web interactions (e.g. search “nightstand drawers”, choose buttons

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: such as “color: modern-nickel-white” or “back to search”). This task is evaluated by average score

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: (percentage of desired attributes covered by the chosen product averaged across all episodes) and

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: success rate (percentage of episodes where the chosen product satisﬁes all requirements) on 500 test

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: instructions. We formulate Act prompts with actions to search, choose product, choose options,

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: and buy, with ReAct prompts additionally reasoning to determine what to explore, when to buy,

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: and what products options are relevant to the instruction. See Table 6 for an example prompt, and

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: Table 10 for model predictions in the Appendix. We compare to an imitation learning (IL) method

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: 5Micheli & Fleuret (2021) ﬁnetuned a GPT-2 model on 3553 task instances and achieved a much improved

chunks.section: experiments showing the potential of ReAct to improve with additional training data. Scaling up
chunks.text: performance than BUTLER, but it is trained on all task types, thus not included as a baseline.
